_strings.@@7f4522257115: Rural Physician Credit — Licensed physicians who practice and reside in a small or rural Alabama community of less than 25,000 residents, with admission privileges to a 'small or rural hospital' having an emergency room (an acute care hospital with less than 105 beds, located more than 20 miles from another acute care facility, or which receives Medicare rural reimbursement from the federal government). Schedule CR must be completed with a copy of the other state's return attached — or W-2Gs if the taxing state does not allow a return to be filed for gambling winnings. The 2025 Schedule OC instructions add an explicit NOTE: residents who worked and received income/wages from a state that has NO income tax are not eligible. _strings.@@e384d2311cfb: 2025 Alabama Form 40NR Booklet (Nonresidents Only, Forms and Instructions), 'Which Form To File' (p. 5): 'You MUST Use Form 40NR If:' — 'You are not a resident of Alabama and you received taxable income from Alabama sources or for performing services within Alabama and your gross income from Alabama sources exceeds the allowable prorated personal exemption, or filing Married Filing Joint under the "Military Spouses Residency Relief Act."' | 2025 Form 40NR Booklet (Nonresidents) — independent second pass on the filing-threshold chart (same $4,500/$8,200/$11,500/$5,750), the sliding Standard Deduction chart (same amounts and the same printed MFJ typo), the identical tax-table figures (e.g. $4,100-$4,200 row = $168 single / $146 MFJ; $16,000-$16,100 = $763/$723; $99,900-$100,000 = $4,958/$4,918), the identical Over $100,000.00 worksheet constants ($4,958.00 / $4,918.00), and the Foreign Income Exclusion text ('All foreign income must be reported on your return, in order to receive any foreign income exclusion' — IRC sec. 911 exclusion via federal Form 2555 only, reported as a negative line 8 entry, no treaty mechanism)
_strings.@@e69d4fd07dfd: Treaty conformity — AL does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by AL. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Alabama does NOT start the return from federal adjusted gross income. Both the resident Form 40 and the nonresident Form 40NR build Alabama income from their own line items computed under Alabama law (2025 Form 40 line 5b wages/salaries/tips from Schedule W-2 line 18 column I plus column J, line 6 interest and dividends, line 7 other income; Form 40NR equivalents), not by importing a federal AGI figure. Because the federal-AGI-conformity flow-through does not exist here, a treaty exclusion that is already netted out of federal AGI does NOT automatically carry to the Alabama return. The 2025 Form 40NR booklet (25f40nrbk.pdf, Other Income / Foreign Income Exclusion) is explicit on the only foreign-income mechanism it recognizes: 'All foreign income must be reported on your return, in order to receive any foreign income exclusion,' and that exclusion is the IRC sec. 911 foreign EARNED income exclusion, claimed as a negative entry on line 8 Other Income with federal Form 2555 attached. There is NO Alabama line, schedule, or instruction that recognizes or excludes income exempt under a U.S. income-TAX TREATY. Given (a) the separate Alabama income build-up rather than a federal-AGI start, and (b) the affirmative report-all-foreign-income rule with only a sec. 911-style exclusion path, conformity to federal treaty exemptions is NOT established on any .gov page. Per conservative handling this is set false and flagged. See unverified/notes.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 40, line 17: 'Income Tax due. Enter amount from tax table or check if from Form NOL-85A' (line 16: 'Taxable income. Subtract line 15 from line 10.'); booklet Line 17 Figuring Your Tax (p.10): 'You must figure your tax from the Tax Tables unless you are claiming a carryover or carryback Net Operating Loss from another year.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 UNCHANGED: the 2025 booklet's What's New page carries only credits and income exclusions (Identity Quiz notice; new-vehicle loan interest deduction under Sec. 40-18-15 for 2025-2028; expanded military-pay exemption, Act 2024-0170; Sound Money Tax Neutrality Act, Act 2024-0447, excluding net capital gains on precious metal bullion beginning January 1, 2025; Alabama Workforce Housing Tax Credit, Act 2024-302; Childcare Facility / Employer / Employer Provider credits, Act 2024-303) — the 2%/4%/5% dual schedules, the sliding standard deduction chart, the $1,500/$3,000 personal exemptions, the income-tiered dependent exemption, and the over-$100,000 worksheet constants were each RE-VERIFIED from the 2025 prints (booklet, printed Form 40, and 40NR booklet), not assumed. Base guidance: Supply 2025 Alabama Form 40, page 1, line 16 'Taxable income. Subtract line 15 from line 10.' Alabama does NOT start from federal AGI: line 10 Alabama adjusted gross income is built from Alabama line items (line 8 total income minus line 9 adjustments), and line 15 total deductions = line 11 (itemized OR sliding standard deduction) + line 12 (FEDERAL income tax deduction, from the Federal Income Tax Deduction Worksheet) + line 13 (personal exemption $1,500/$3,000) + line 14 (income-dependent dependent exemption). All of those subtractions must already be taken on the form before line 16 — this op subtracts nothing further. Tax-table mandate: the 2025 Form 40 booklet (Line 17 Figuring Your Tax, p.10) states 'You must figure your tax from the Tax Tables unless you are claiming a carryover or carryback Net Operating Loss from another year.' The Tax Tables (booklet pp. 25-30) cover taxable income under $100,000 in $100-wide bands priced at the band midpoint, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within a table band (booklet example: MFJ $23,360 -> table $1,088, which equals exact bracket math at that figure); the filed form must use the table. Over $100,000: the 2025 booklet's worksheet (p. 30) computes tax as $4,958.00 (Single/Married filing separately/Head of family) or $4,918.00 (Married filing jointly) plus 5% of taxable income over $100,000 — both constants re-derived for 2025 and unchanged. Those printed constants are each $2 LESS than the exact cumulative bracket sums ($4,960 = 500x.02 + 2,500x.04 + 97,000x.05; $4,920 = 1,000x.02 + 5,000x.04 + 94,000x.05) because they carry forward the last tax-table row's midpoint value (the $99,900-$100,000 row prints $4,958/$4,918); at and above $100,000 the tax the form produces is therefore $2 lower than this op's pure bracket math. FEDERAL income tax deduction quirk: Alabama allows a base deduction for federal income tax liability (Form 40 line 12; Federal Income Tax Deduction Worksheet, 2025 booklet: 2025 Form 1040/1040-SR/1040NR line 22 plus Form 8960 line 17 net investment income tax, minus refundable EIC, Additional Child Tax Credit, American Opportunity Credit, and Form 2439 credits). It is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes — do not re-subtract it. standard_deduction is NOT shipped because Alabama's standard deduction slides with Alabama AGI (2025 booklet p. 9 chart, amounts unchanged from 2024): MFJ $8,500 (AL AGI $0-$25,999) phasing down to $5,000 at $35,500 and above; MFS $4,250 ($0-$12,999) down to $2,500 at $17,750 and above; Head of Family $5,200 ($0-$25,999) down to $2,500 at $35,500 and above; Single $3,000 ($0-$25,999) down to $2,500 at $35,500 and above. Take it from the chart on Form 40 line 11; it is already inside line 16. (Both 2025 booklets reprint the same MFJ third-band typo '$25,500 - $26,999' for what the surrounding rows show is $26,500 - $26,999 — see the pack's unverified list.) Personal exemption (Form 40 line 13) is $1,500 (Single or Married Filing Separately) / $3,000 (Married Filing Jointly or Head of Family), printed on the 2025 Form 40 filing-status boxes 1-4 (box 4 now adds 'Complete Schedule HOF'). It is a base reduction, but it is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes, so it is NOT shipped as an engine exemption. Dependent exemption (Form 40 line 14, from page 2 Part III line 2) is income-dependent and NOT shipped: $1,000 per dependent when the amount on page 1, line 10 is $0-$50,000; $500 when $50,001-$100,000; $300 when over $100,000 (2025 booklet p. 10 chart, unchanged from 2024). It is already inside line 16 — claim it on the form, not through this op. One rate schedule covers Single, Married Filing Separately, and Head of Family (2% on the first $500, 4% on the next $2,500, 5% over $3,000); Married Filing Jointly has its own schedule (2% on the first $1,000, 4% on the next $5,000, 5% over $6,000). Alabama has no qualifying-surviving-spouse filing status (Form 40 boxes are Single / Married filing joint / Married filing separate / Head of Family, and the 2025 booklet's Head of Family definition requires that the individual 'is not a surviving spouse' and that the qualifying dependent is not a foster child). The engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping does not correspond to an Alabama status — a filer widowed before 2025 files Single or Head of Family in Alabama, so do not rely on the MFJ schedule for a federal QSS filer. TY2025 WAGE-BASE CAVEAT (outside the rate schedule): the Alabama overtime exemption (Act 2023-421 as amended by Act 2024-437) ENDED June 30, 2025 per the ADOR notice of May 29, 2025, so TY2025 wages include only a HALF-YEAR of exempt overtime — reported in W-2 Box 14 as 'EX OT WAGES' and excluded from Box 16 state wages. That affects the Form 40 line 5b wage figure the caller builds line 16 from; this op models only the rate schedule. This op computes the state rate-schedule line only. Alabama credits (Schedule OC), the consumer use tax and Catastrophe Savings tax reported on Schedule ATP (Form 40 line 19), and the Alabama Election Campaign Fund contributions (lines 20a/20b) are NOT modeled.
